title: How a PeopleSoft page is put together
body:
PeopleSoft's web pages (PIA) come in two kinds.

- **Classic pages** are shown inside the portal: the header and menus are one page, and the component (the page you test) is in an iframe, `id="ptifrmtgtframe"`, `name="TargetContent"`. Locators must go through the frame: `page.frame_locator("#ptifrmtgtframe")`.
- **Fluid pages** (PeopleTools 8.54 and later) usually aren't in that iframe; but their modal dialogs are often iframes of their own.

Which kind a component is shows in its URL and in the page: when in doubt, look for `#ptifrmtgtframe` in the page.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: URLs: /psp/ and /psc/
body: A component's URL looks like `/psp/SITE/PORTAL/NODE/c/MENU.COMPONENT.GBL` (for example `/psp/ps/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/ADMINISTER_WORKFORCE.JOB_DATA.GBL`). `psp` is the portal: header plus the TargetContent frame. The same path with `psc` instead (`/psc/ps/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/...`) serves the component **alone, with no frame**. For tests of one component, going straight to the `/psc/` URL removes the frame from every locator. Query parameters such as `?Page=PAGENAME&Action=U` (update) or `A` (add) open a given page and mode; whether they're honoured depends on the component.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Element ids: RECORD_FIELD$row
body:
Fields have stable ids built from the record and field: `JOB_EMPLID`, and with a row number in scrolls and grids: `JOB_EMPLID$0`, `JOB_DEPTID$1` (rows count from 0). Buttons and links follow the same pattern. They don't change between sessions, which makes them better than generated or positional selectors.

The `$` in these ids isn't valid in a plain CSS `#id` selector: use an attribute selector, `[id='JOB_EMPLID$0']`, or escape it, `#JOB_EMPLID\$0`. Labels are usually real `<label for=...>`, so `get_by_label("Empl ID")` also works, but in grids several rows share a label: prefer the id with its row number there.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Server round trips: wait for processing
body: Changing a field can run PeopleCode on the server (FieldEdit and FieldChange), which fires when the field changes **and loses focus**. So after `fill`, press Tab (or click elsewhere), then wait for the page to finish: the processing indicator (in classic pages `#WAIT_win0`; check what your pages show while busy) appears during the trip and hides after. Never wait a fixed time: wait for the indicator to hide, then for the field the PeopleCode changes. Clicking a button that saves, searches or changes the page is a round trip too.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Toolbar buttons and message boxes: ids that start with #
body:
In classic pages the toolbar buttons have ids that **include a #**: `#ICSave` (Save), `#ICList` (Return to Search), `#ICNextInList` and `#ICPrevInList`, and on search pages `#ICSearch`. A CSS selector `#ICSave` looks for an id "ICSave" and finds nothing: use `[id='#ICSave']`.

Messages (saved, warnings, errors) appear as a message box whose OK button is `[id='#ICOK']` (and Cancel `[id='#ICCancel']` where there is one). Depending on the version the box may be inside a modal iframe (`#ptModFrame_0`, numbered from 0): go through `frame_locator` when it is. Read the message text before closing it: it's often the thing to assert.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Search pages
body: Most classic components open on a search page: fill its keys, then `[id='#ICSearch']`. One match opens the component; several show a results grid to click; none shows a "no matching values" message. Going to the component's URL with its keys (where the component allows it) skips the search page.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Signing in, once
body: The sign-on page is at `/psp/SITE/?cmd=login`, with fields `#userid` and `#pwd` and a submit button (`input[name=Submit]` on many versions). Sign in once per test run and reuse the session: save it with `context.storage_state(path="auth.json")` and start each test's context with `storage_state="auth.json"`. Credentials come from environment variables, never the test file. Sessions time out (server-side settings): a long run may need to sign in again.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version

title: Writing tests that last
body:
- Test against a development or test environment, never production.
- One browser context per test; test data the test creates itself, or known fixed data.
- Locate by stable id (`RECORD_FIELD$row`) or label; never by position or layout classes.
- After every action that goes to the server: wait for processing to finish, then assert with `expect(...)` (it retries).
- Record traces in CI (`context.tracing.start(screenshots=True, snapshots=True)`); open a failure with `playwright show-trace trace.zip`.
- `playwright codegen URL` records clicks as code: start it on the `/psc/` URL to keep the frame out of the recorded selectors.
source: general PeopleSoft knowledge: verify on your PeopleTools version
